study.title: An fMRI Study of Neuronal Specificity in Acupuncture: The Multiacupoint Siguan and Its Sham Point
study.study_design: Single block experimental design, between-subjects comparison of real versus sham acupuncture
study.randomization: Subjects were randomly divided into real acupoint (21 subjects) and sham acupoint (10 subjects) groups
study.population: Thirty-one healthy volunteers (14 men, 17 women; age range: 45–75 years; mean: 61.7 ± 7.9 years; all right-handed)
study.inclusion_criteria: (a) no neurological or psychiatric disorders such as stroke, depression, or epilepsy; (b) no neurological deficiencies such as visual or hearing loss; (c) no cognitive complaints; (d) no contraindications for MRI; and (e) no abnormal findings such as infarctions or focal lesions from conventional brain MRI
study.exclusion_criteria: (a) incapable of enduring pain or other physiology reaction caused by acupuncture stimulation and (b) severe head motion during scanning

conditions.scan_context: Resting-state fMRI, eyes closed, instructed to stay awake, hold still, keep eyes closed, and think nothing in particular
conditions.tissue_level_reasoning: Needles inserted superficially to a depth of less than 5 mm; no manipulation and no current stimulation performed

conditions.timepoint_exact: 3 min during acupuncture stimulation (after 3 min baseline)
conditions.scan_context: fMRI acquired during acupuncture needle insertion and rotation at Siguan (bilateral LI4 and Liv3)

conditions.timepoint_exact: 3 min during acupuncture stimulation (after 3 min baseline)
conditions.scan_context: fMRI acquired during acupuncture needle insertion and rotation at sham points (10 mm anterior to Liv3 or LI4)
conditions.tissue_level_reasoning: Needle is explicitly inserted to a depth of 2 cm (20 mm), which far exceeds the 5 mm threshold for full penetration. At this depth the needle reaches muscle/fascia and engages deep mechanoreceptors. The only sham element is the non-acupoint location (~10 mm anterior to real points); the physical tissue engagement is equivalent to real acupuncture.

conditions.scan_context: fMRI acquired after needles were withdrawn

interventions.procedure_label_exact: Manual acupuncture at Siguan (bilateral LI4 and Liv3)
interventions.anatomical_location_exact: Taichong (Liv3): on the dorsum of the left and right feet, in the depression anterior to the junction of the first and second metatarsals; Hegu (LI4): on the dorsum of the left and right hands, at the midpoint on the radial side of the second metacarpal
interventions.needle_size_exact: 0.3 mm in diameter and 25 mm long
interventions.manipulation_exact: needles rotated continuously (±180°, 60 times per minute)
interventions.session_duration_exact: 16-min total scan time; 3 min baseline, 3 min stimulation, 10 min post-needle withdrawal
interventions.practitioner_description_exact: same two skilled acupuncturists in synchrony
interventions.participant_instructions_exact: stay awake, hold still, keep eyes closed, and think nothing in particular
interventions.treatment_rationale_given_exact: Siguan has been conventionally used for several symptoms, especially those of gastrointestinal and neurological disorders

interventions.procedure_label_exact: Manual acupuncture at sham acupoints (10 mm anterior to Liv3 or LI4)
interventions.anatomical_location_exact: sham acupoints located approximately 10 mm anterior to the corresponding real ones (Liv3 and LI4)
interventions.needle_size_exact: 0.3 mm in diameter and 25 mm long
interventions.manipulation_exact: needles rotated continuously (±180°, 60 times per minute)
interventions.session_duration_exact: 16-min total scan time; 3 min baseline, 3 min stimulation, 10 min post-needle withdrawal
interventions.practitioner_description_exact: same two skilled acupuncturists in synchrony
interventions.participant_instructions_exact: stay awake, hold still, keep eyes closed, and think nothing in particular
interventions.treatment_rationale_given_exact: sham point design that entails needling at the same depth and with the same pattern but at a nonacupoint located 10 millimeters away from the real one

sham_details.sham_subtype_exact: nonacupoint needling at same depth and same manipulation pattern
sham_details.sham_penetration_exact: penetrating, inserted to depth of 2 cm
sham_details.sham_location_exact: approximately 10 mm anterior to the corresponding real acupoints (Liv3 and LI4)
sham_details.sham_manipulation_exact: needles rotated continuously (±180°, 60 times per minute)

sensory_interoceptive_responses.notes: Sensory/deqi responses were not measured or reported in this study. No sensation questionnaire or deqi instrument was administered.

neuroimaging_methods.voxel_size_exact: 3 × 3 × 3 mm (after reslicing); original: 64 × 64 matrix, 3 mm thickness, 1 mm gap
neuroimaging_methods.normalization_template_exact: standard EPI template via their corresponding mean images; Talairach stereotaxic space
neuroimaging_methods.smoothing_exact: Gaussian filter of 6-mm full-width at half maximum
neuroimaging_methods.motion_exclusion_exact: corrected for motion; severe head motion was an exclusion criterion
primary_neuroimaging_metrics: BOLD fMRI activation (impulse response functions modeled as summation of tent-basis functions)
statistical_thresholds_exact: minimum cluster sizes were 17 voxels (459 mm3), and the maximum P value for voxels was 0.01. All surviving voxels had an adjusted P value < 0.05
neuroimaging_methods.multiple_comparison_correction_exact: AlphaSim correction; minimum cluster sizes 17 voxels (459 mm3), maximum P value 0.01, all surviving voxels adjusted P < 0.05

contrasts.contrast_label_exact: Brain regions activated by acupuncture stimulation at the real acupoint (Siguan) (compared with the resting-state)
contrasts.contrast_type_exact: real acupuncture stimulation > baseline resting-state (within arm_real)
contrasts.analysis_method_exact: First-level: 3dDeconvolve (tent-basis functions, 20 TRs/60 s post-stimulation); second-level random-effects analysis
contrasts.statistical_model_exact: random-effects analysis with tent-basis function deconvolution
contrasts.thresholding_method_exact: AlphaSim correction; minimum cluster sizes 17 voxels (459 mm3), maximum P value 0.01

contrasts.contrast_label_exact: Brain regions activated by acupuncture stimulation at the sham acupoint (compared with the resting-state)
contrasts.contrast_type_exact: sham acupuncture stimulation > baseline resting-state (within arm_sham)
contrasts.analysis_method_exact: First-level: 3dDeconvolve (tent-basis functions, 20 TRs/60 s post-stimulation); second-level random-effects analysis
contrasts.statistical_model_exact: random-effects analysis with tent-basis function deconvolution
contrasts.thresholding_method_exact: AlphaSim correction; minimum cluster sizes 17 voxels (459 mm3), maximum P value 0.01

contrasts.contrast_label_exact: Brain regions activated more by stimulation at the real acupoint than by stimulation at the sham acupoint
contrasts.contrast_type_exact: real acupuncture > sham acupuncture (between-group two-sample t-test)
contrasts.analysis_method_exact: Two-sample t-tests between data from real and sham acupoint groups; second-level random-effects analysis
contrasts.thresholding_method_exact: AlphaSim correction; minimum cluster sizes 17 voxels (459 mm3), maximum P value 0.01
contrasts.direction_exact: real > sham (greater activation for real acupuncture)

contrasts.thresholding_method_exact: p<0.05 AlphaSim correction, minimum cluster size 17 voxels (459 mm3), maximum voxel-level p<0.01
contrasts._sham_description: Non-acupoint needling at four sham points located approximately 10 mm anterior to the corresponding real Siguan acupoints (Liv3 and LI4), using the same stainless non-magnetic needles (0.3 mm diameter, 25 mm long), inserted to 2 cm depth with continuous rotation (±180°, 60 times per minute)

funding_conflicts_registration.conflict_of_interest_exact: The authors declare that there is no conflict of interests regarding the publication of this paper.

extraction_notes.note: Sensory/deqi responses were not assessed or reported. No sensation questionnaire, VAS pain scale, or deqi instrument was mentioned anywhere in the paper.
Expectancy, credibility, blinding success, and allocation guessing were not assessed or reported.
Adverse events were not reported; no statement about safety or adverse events during scanning or acupuncture was provided.
Funding sources were not reported in the paper.
Ethics approval information was not explicitly stated in the text, though informed consent was mentioned.

The paper notes additional regions activated by whole-cluster consideration beyond peak voxel labeling (e.g., right superior medial prefrontal gyrus BA10, right calcarine gyrus, bilateral precuneus for real acupoint; right anterior and middle cingulate cortices for sham; right precuneus BA23, right fusiform gyrus, left putamen, right mid-orbital gyrus, bilateral rectal gyrus BA11, left inferior temporal gyrus for real>sham contrast). These are described in the Results text but not separately tabulated with coordinates; they are captured via the primary table row clusters.

The asterisk notation in Tables 1 and 2 (e.g., 'Middle occipital gyrus*', 'Cerebellum (VIII)*', 'Insula*') indicates peak voxels located in white matter; the labeled region reflects where most voxels in the cluster were located. This is noted in table footnotes.
The contrast_real_vs_sham (Table 3) does not include the sham > real direction. The paper does not report brain regions more activated by sham than by real acupuncture.

The paper states 31 subjects total were analyzed for neuroimaging (21 real + 10 sham). The n_analyzed for the between-group contrast (real > sham) is inferred as 31 (all subjects), as both groups contribute to the two-sample t-test.

The paper uses a single block design: 3 min baseline, 3 min stimulation, 10 min post-withdrawal. The impulse response function was modeled for 20 TRs (60 s) after stimulation onset. It is unclear whether the reported activation reflects the stimulation period alone or extends into the post-stimulation period.

No flip angle is listed for the structural T1 sequence: the paper states FA 90° for the EPI functional sequence but also writes FA 90° in the structural sequence description (TR, 1900 ms; TE, 2.2 ms; TI, 900 ms; FA, 90°). This may be an OCR or typographical error in the original paper, as MPRAGE sequences typically use a small flip angle.
Deactivation results (reduced brain activity) were not reported or analyzed, as acknowledged by the authors in the Discussion as a study limitation.
No single acupoint stimulation arm was included; the paper acknowledges this as a limitation.
